newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslems block traffic in protest.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslems block traffic in protest.

text.p: More than 250 Bosnian Moslem civilians blocked traffic in the north of the country in two separate incidents on Monday in protest against the situation in the village of Jusici, NATO said in an official statement.
About 130 Moslems recently occupied Jusici, which lies just inside Bosnia's Serb republic. Some of the Moslems were legitimate refugees driven from their homes by war and others were armed.

NATO peace forces confiscated and destroyed weapons in the village and, along with other international representatives, have been pressuring the Moslems to leave Jusici and re-apply for permission to re-enter.
Moslem leaders and local residents have rejected that appeal, which they say would diminish their rights under the Dayton peace treaty which ended their country's 43-month war.
NATO's statement said about 150 Moslems had blocked traffic near the tunnel on the main road between Tuzla and Kalesija on Monday.
The statement also reported that more than 100 Moslem blocked traffic and threw stones at passing vehicles southeast of Simin Han. Both demonstrations were tied to Jusici.
NATO despatched military police and civil affairs teams to provide assistance to U.N. and local Bosnian police if required. There were no reports of injuries or damage.
